headline: Continued Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code hearing to October 13, approved SKHA PILOT agreement and several contracts including portable radios and road salt.
summary: The Town Council held a work session on the ESKAPE bike-pedestrian corridor plan and heard a public hearing on proposed Form-Based Code zoning amendments for Old Tower Hill Road, continuing the hearing to October 13, 2026. The Council also approved a PILOT agreement for South Kingstown Housing Authority properties, various licenses, tax abatements, a pole-setting petition, contracts for salt and radios, a school facility agreement, and voted to authorize advertising a public hearing on prohibiting data centers in Industrial Zones.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 14, 2026 Regular Session.
Accepted the minutes of the September 14, 2026 Closed Executive Session.
Approved the Consent Agenda items.
Authorized a tax abatement of $23,532.98 under Tax Abatement Request No. 667.
Granted Rhode Island Energy's petition #13955336 to install two new terminal riser poles on Plains Road.
Granted Victualling License renewals for five businesses including Taste of Korea and Falafel Dave's.
Granted a Victualling and Additional Hours License renewal for Tower Hill Donuts, Inc. d/b/a Dunkin Donuts.
Granted a Temporary Mass Gathering Permit for Oktoberfest at Birch and Bay on October 17, 2026.
Granted a Temporary Mass Gathering Permit for the Arts & Eats event at Sons of Liberty on October 17, 2026.
Continued the Public Hearing on the Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code zoning amendments to October 13, 2026.
Adopted a proclamation thanking poll workers and Town staff for the September 2026 Primary Election.
Authorized the Town Manager to sign an updated PILOT agreement for SKHA properties at Champagne Heights, Fournier Estates, and Village Gardens.
Continued the NEOGOV Perform software contract authorization to a future meeting.
Continued the Potter's Farm Homeowners Association bike path maintenance agreement authorization to a future meeting.
Authorized the Town Manager to execute a Memorandum of Agreement with the School District for shared use of the School Maintenance Facility at 135 Asa Pond Road.
Authorized an award to Mid-American Salt, LLC for Solar Salt at $77.17 per ton.
Authorized an award to Marcus Communications for portable radios not to exceed $25,562.90.
Authorized the Town Clerk to advertise a Public Hearing on amendments to prohibit data centers in Industrial Zones.
Received and referred a letter on preserving the Oliver Watson House to the Planning Department.
Received and placed on file an email on funding consulting services for North-South Bicycle Pedestrian Corridors.
Received and placed on file an email from Veronika Kot on the Form-Based Code amendments.
Received and placed on file an email from Melissa Towle on the Form-Based Code amendments.
Continued an email on regional desalination to October 13, 2026.
Received, placed on file, and referred a banner request to RIDOT.
Received, placed on file, and referred a request to tie ribbons on Main Street to the Town Manager.

REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
1 
At a REGULAR SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of 
Washington, in the State of Rhode Island held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 28th day 
of September 2026 at 6:05 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
1. A. CLOSED EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to recess to Closed Executive Session pursuant to §42 -46-5(a)(5) 
pertaining to the acquisition or lease of real property for public purposes and RIGL §42-46-5(a)(2) to 
discuss and/or act upon matters pertaining to litigation, including Maine v. The Union Fire District of 
South Kingstown, WC-2026-0479.  
 
Regular Session is reconvened at 7:05 PM. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to seal the minutes of Closed Executive Session pursuant to §42-46-
5(a)(5) pertaining to the acquisition or lease of real property for public purposes and RIGL §42-46-
5(a)(2) to discuss and/or act upon matters pertaining to litigation, including Maine v. The Union Fire 
District of South Kingstown, WC-2026-0479. 
 
Andrew Teitz, Town Solicitor, notes that one vote was taken in Executive Session. 
 
 
Emily R. Houle 
Town Clerk
WORK SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
2 
 
At a WORK SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of Washington, 
in the State of Rhode Island, held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 28th day of September 
2026 at 7:10 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
2. A. WORK SESSION  
 
Ken Burke, Bicycle-Pedestrian Advisory Committee (BPAC) Member, introduces a presentation 
relating to the Experience South Kingstown Access Path for Everyone (ESKAPE) Plan to connect 
access paths across Route 1 from north to south in the area of Salt Pond Road through Ministerial 
Road. ESKAPE has been under review from multiple agencies both locally and statewide, and would 
promote safety, economic development, health, and recreation. 
 
ESKAPE is intended to identify encumbrances and best practice to reinstate north-south corridors. 
Neighboring communities have instituted safety measures such as the installation of modern traffic 
signals on Route 1 to slow traffic and provide access with the assistance of the RI Department of 
Transportation (RIDOT). The BPAC is requesting funding in the amount of $50,000 through the 
Capital Improvement Program (CIP) to engage a professional engineering firm to consult on optimal 
corridor connections. 
 
Neil Murray, BPAC Member, explains the importance of connecting villages from north to south as 
currently exists from east to west, and outlines potential challenges.  
 
Shane Jones, BPAC Member, comments on the importance of accessing Matunuck via bicycle. 
 
Lisa Beth Sanford, BPAC Secretary, explains the need for a feasibility study to identify appropriate 
crossing areas and thanks the Council for allowing consideration of the plan. 
 
Ken Burke notes the support of other communities, organizations, and Town staff including Lucas 
Murray, Deputy Town M anager/DOAS, Richard Bourbonnais, Public Services Director, James 
Rabbitt, Planning Director, and Theresa Murphy, Director of Leisure Services. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to expanding bicycle-pedestrian corridors to include other areas of Town, 
the need to set achie vable milestones and short-term goals to measure progress, the requested 
funding amount of $50,000, the timeline for the project, and preparation of an RFP. 
 
Convened to Regular Session. 
 
 
Emily R. Houle 
Town Clerk
REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
3 
 
At a REGULAR SESSION of the Town Council of the Town of South Kingstown, County of 
Washington, in the State of Rhode Island held at the Town Hall, in and for said Town on the 28th day 
of September 2026 at 7:44 PM. 
 
 PRESENT: Rory H. McEntee, President  
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
 
3. REGULAR SESSION  
 
A. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  
 
The Pledge of Allegiance is given. 
 
B. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT  
 
The Land Acknowledgement Statement is read. 
 
4. ROLL CALL 
 
Roll Call is taken. Council Vice President Marran is absent. 
 
5. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETINGS 
 
A. Regular Session: UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: that the minutes of the Regular Session held 
on September 14, 2026 are accepted, approved, and placed on file. 
 
C. Closed Executive Session: UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: that the minutes of the Closed 
Executive Session held on September 14, 2026 are accepted. 
 
8. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to approve the Consent Agenda as indicated by (CA) on same. 
 
(CA) A. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Assessor to abate taxes in the 
amount of $23,532.98, as shown on Tax Abatement Request No. 667. 
 
(CA) B. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant Petition #13955336 of Rhode Island Energy to 
install two (2) new terminal riser poles, P17 & P18, on the east side of Plains Road just south of its 
intersection with West Alumni Avenue. A request was made by the University of Rhode Island to use 
the public ways named for the purposes stated in said petition, that the work be done to the 
satisfaction of the Director of Public Services and notification to the Town for municipal utility mark-
out prior to pole setting, and that this approval is conditioned upon the removal of all existing double 
poles along the entire length of Plains Road prior to new pole(s) placement; and any new double 
poles created as part of this request be removed within sixty (60) calendar days of new pole(s) 
placement. Said petition is further described in a memorandum from the Public Services Director to 
the Town Manager dated September 17, 2026, and entitled, "Rhode Island Energy Pole Setting 
Request - Poles P17 & P18 Plains Road." Book 6, Page 36.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
4 
 
(CA) C. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant Victualling Licenses for the year beginning 
December 1, 2026 to the following; Renewals: 
 
Jinwoong Kim d/b/a Taste of Korea, 99 Fortin Road, Kingston, RI 02881. Application by Jinwoong 
Kim, Owner; License No. 89951. 
 
Falafel Daves Corp d/b/a Falafel Dave’s, 203 Main Street, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application by Carla 
Boutros, Owner; License No. 92723. 
 
72 Old Tower LLC d/b/a Mobil, 72 Old Tower Hill Road, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application by 
Ankitkumar Patel, Member; License No. 84353. 
 
Taylors Landing Country Store, Inc. d/b/a TLC Coffee Roasters, 3362 Kingstown Road, West 
Kingston, RI 02892. Application by James McCarthy, Vice President; License No. 81647.  
 
South County Donuts, Inc. d/b/a Dunkin Donuts, 231 Old Tower Hill Road, Wakefield, RI 02879. 
Application by Rob Batista, President; License No. 64574. 
 
(CA) D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant Victualling and Additional Hours Licenses for the 
year beginning December 1, 2026 to Tower Hill Donuts, Inc. d/b/a Dunkin Donuts, 3045 Tower Hill 
Road, Wakefield, RI 02879. Application by Angela Moroney, Office Administrator. Renewal; License 
No. 86019. 
 
9. LICENSES 
 
A. John Brito and Stephen Fox are present and after testimony and discussion it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Temporary Mass Gathering Permit to conduct Oktoberfest on 
October 17, 2026, from 11:00 am to 11:00 pm at Birch and Bay, 323 Main Street, Wakefield, RI 
02879 and on Main Street between Robinson Street and Kenyon Avenue, subject to RI Department 
of Transportation approval for the closure of Main Street and stipulations set by the Police 
Department and Building Official, and the execution of a hold harmless agreement indemnifying the 
Town and receipt of a Certificate of Insurance naming the Town as an additional insured for the event 
in the amounts specified by the Finance Director. Application by John Brito, Owner. New; License 
No. TMG-26-8. 
 
B. Paul Baptista is present and after testimony and discussion it is 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to grant a Temporary Mass Gathering Permit to Sons of Liberty, 1425 
Kingstown Road, Wakefield, RI 02879 to conduct the annual fall Arts & Eats event on Saturday, 
October 17, 2026 from 12:00 PM to 6:00 PM. Application by Paul Baptista, Member. New; License 
No. TMG-26-6. 
 
10. PUBLIC COMMENTS – 30 Minutes 
 
Council President McEntee invites residents to come forward with comments. 
 
Jennifer Nerbonne, First Chair of the South Kingstown Republican Party Committee, comments on 
appointments to the Canvassing Authority, infrastructure projects, and proper representation by 
elected officials.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
5 
 
Jim O’Neill comments on Affordable Housing legislation and concerns about State overreach in local 
government. 
 
Ken Swain, Chairman of the Affordable Housing Collaborative Committee, comments on the function 
of the Affordable Housing Fund. 
 
11. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
A. Council President McEntee notes that due to the Vice President’s absence, no vote will be 
taken in the Public Hearing. 
 
James Rabbitt, Planning Director, begins a presentation on proposed Form-Based Code (FBC) 
Zoning Amendments. He reviews a timeline of FBC development and FBC as a regulatory tool as it 
relates to traffic. 
 
Discussion ensues. 
 
The Planning Director continues relative to storm water management and regulation by the RI 
Department of Environmental Management (RIDEM), when FBC standards apply, FBC text sections, 
uses presently allowed in existing Zoning districts, and uses removed or introduce d under FBC 
residential districts FB1: Residential Neighborhood and FB1.5: Neighborhood Edge. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to the residential districts. 
 
The Planning Director continues to review uses allowed in districts FB2: Neighborhood Center, FB3: 
Neighborhood Core, and FB4: Route 1 Transition.  
 
Discussion ensues relative to permitted uses and expansion of existing non-conforming properties. 
 
The Planning Director continues relative to FBC development of streets and civic spaces. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to use protection offered by FBC  and potentially removing larger 
residential uses from FB1 or adding limiting language to current residential Zoning districts. 
 
Council President McEntee invites the residents to come forward with comments. 
 
Geoff Levy, Wakefield Mall owner, comments in opposition to FBC as proposed. 
 
William McGowan comments in opposition to FBC and proposes to limit short-term rentals instead. 
 
Melissa Towle comments in opposition of the FBC residential districts. 
 
Matthew Landry, Esq. comments on behalf of Scot Hallberg and Costanza Realty LLC relative to 
inconsistencies in the FBC text regulations. 
 
Larry Fish comments on the development of FBC during his time on the Economic Development 
Committee (EDC) and in opposition to FBC as currently proposed. 
 
Barbara Lema comments in opposition to FBC.
REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
6 
 
Elizabeth Scott comments on stormwater management. 
 
Joe Viele requests clarification for expansion of non-conforming uses. 
 
The Town Solicitor responds. 
 
Michael Gagas, EDC Chair, comments in favor of FBC. 
 
There being no other comments it is  
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to continue to October 13, 2026 a Public Hearing to consider proposed 
amendments to the Zoning Ordinance, Appendix A: Article 6, New Section 610, to implement Old 
Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code (FBC) and establish five (5) Form-Based Districts, as shown on 
the attached Regulating Plan Map and viewable i n its entirety on the Town's website 
at: https://www.southkingstownri.gov/othr-fbc. 
 
The FBC  provides a regulatory framework that supports a walkable, mixed -use, and context -
sensitive suburban/urban environment in the Old Tower Hill Road area. The amendments set forth 
when the FBC standards apply, define the scope of compliance with those standards, and establish 
the review process and  application requirements for development applications within the FBC 
Districts. 
 
12. NEW BUSINESS 
 
B. Council President McEntee reads the proclamation into the record. 
 
Walter Young, Jr, Canvassing Authority Chair, is present and comments on the election work 
performed by Town staff and the Board of Canvassers. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to adopt a proclamation expressing gratitude to Poll Workers and Town 
Staff for their service during the September 9, 2026 Primary Election, as requested by Canvassing 
Authority Chair Walter Young, Jr., as follows: 
 
PROCLAMATION 
 
IN APPRECIATION AND GRATITUDE TO POLL WORKERS & STAFF FOR SERVICE 
DURING THE SEPTEMBER 2026 PRIMARY ELECTION 
 
WHEREAS,  voting is a precious American principle; a basic Democratic right for our 
people, which should be protected, promoted, and practiced; and 
 
WHEREAS,  on our most recent Primary Election Day of September 9, 2026, many in 
the Town of South Kingstown nobly offered to serve our residents throughout 20 days of 
early voting and on election day and uphold this foundational democratic institution for our 
community; and 
 
WHEREAS,  staff in the Town Clerk’s office provided commendable, tireless, and 
flexible service to our community to maintain voter records, ensure security and compliance 
with election laws, and oversee the election process; and
REGULAR SESSION 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
7 
 
WHEREAS,  the Town employed over 60 poll workers representing a diverse group of 
local residents to carry out election duties throughout early voting and on election day; and 
WHEREAS,  the South Kingstown Police Department stationed uniformed officers at 
each of the polling locations to provide a visible law enforcement presence to help reassure 
voters that their safety is a priority and maintain a safe and orderly environment; and 
 
WHEREAS, additional Town staff including members of the Facilities and Highway 
Departments assisted the Town Clerk’s office to set up polling locations and provide signage 
in advance and after the election day; and 
 
WHEREAS,  our Town is truly grateful for each of these individuals who contributed 
various duties to the election process to ensure a successful Primary Election; and 
 
NOW THEREFORE WE THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF SOUTH KINGSTOWN 
do hereby offer our appreciation and gratitude to poll workers and staff for service during the 
September 2026 Primary Election. 
 
A. Council President McEntee introduces a request by the South Kingstown Housing Authority 
(SKHA) for an updated PILOT agreement for Champagne Heights, Fournier Estates, and Village 
Gardens. 
 
The Town Solicitor requests that an approval by the Council be subject to the Solicitor’s review. 
 
Chris Little, SKHA Chair, reviews the proposed updated PILOT agreement, an upcoming meeting to 
rename Champagne Heights to honor Cpl. David Champagne, Housing and Urban Development 
(HUD) funding changes that require SKHA properties to be owned by a separate legal entity with 
SKHA maintaining control of the affiliate and land ownership, and planned improvements at the 
properties. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to planned new units and affordable housing tax credits.  
 
Derek Farias, Sokoloff Farias Associates, explains HUD rent calculations. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Manager to sign an updated South Kingstown 
Housing Authority (SKHA) and SKHA Services & Development Corporation PILOT agreement for 
the properties located at Champagne Heights, 364 Curtis Corner Road, Fournier Estates, 480 High 
Street, and Village Gardens, 69 Uncle Sams Lane, subject to review by the Town Solicitor.  
 
C. The Town Manager requests to continue New Business C and D. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to continue to a future meeting authorization of an award of contract to 
GovernmentJobs.com, Inc., d/b/a NEOGOV, 2120 Park Place, Suite 100, El Segundo, CA 90245, 
for the purchase, setup, implementation, and subscription of the NEOGOV Perform performance 
management software module for a term commencing December 31, 2026, and continuing through 
June 30, 2028, in an amount not to exceed twenty thousand one hundred thirty-seven dollars and 
seventy-nine cents ($20,137.79), through Sourcewell Contract No. 030425-PDMS, with funding 
available through the FY 2027 Personnel Administration, Computer / Software Maintenance account, 
as further described in a memorandum from the Deputy Town Manager/DOAS to the Town Manager 
dated September 18, 2026, entitled “Recommendation for Purchase Award – NEOGOV Perform

SEPTEMBER 28, 2026

Performance Management Software.” 
 
D. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to continue to a future meeting authorization for the Town Manager 
to execute a Memorandum of Agreement with the Potter’s Farm Homeowners Association for the 
maintenance of two public bike path connector segments, subject to review and approval by the 
Town Solicitor as to form and substance, as further described in a memorandum from the Deputy

E. Mark Russo, Director of Facilities,  reviews a request for a Memorandum of Agreement

UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Manager to execute a Memorandum of Agreement

UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize an award for the purchase of portable radios to Marcus

H. UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to authorize the Town Clerk to advertise for Order of Notice a 
Public Hearing to consider proposed amendments to the Town's Zoning Ordinance Article 3. Use 
Regulations, Section 301. Schedule of Use Regulations Table., Appendix A. Use Code Descriptions, 
to prohibit data centers in Industrial Zones, as requested by Council Vice President Marran, as 
follows:

 7.0 INDUSTRIAL 
80 Data Center 
 A room, building, structure, facility, or group of facilities designed, constructed, 
or operated as a principal use for the primary purpose of housing computer 
systems, servers, network equipment, and associated infrastructure for the 
storage, processing, transmission, or management of digital data or 
applications, at a scale and intensity substantially greater than that customarily

high-intensity computing operations, whether operated for a single user or 
multiple users, and whether permanent, modular, or temporary in nature.  This 
term does not include server rooms or information technology infrastructure that 
is customarily incidental and subordinate to another permitted principal use.

13. TOWN MANAGER’S REPORT 
 
C. The Town Manager requests to continue Town Manager’s Report C to a future meeting. 
 
A. Emily Houle, Town Clerk, reviews the results of the Primary Election.  
 
B. Theresa Murphy, Director of Leisure Services, reviews parks improvements completed over 
the past two years and planned upcoming projects through the Capital Improvement Program (CIP). 
 
D. The Town Manager reviews the Veolia water ban and notes that it is moving to an odd/even 
schedule. Representatives of Veolia were invited to the Town Council meeting but did not respond. 
 
The Town Solicitor  notes that during the Closed Executive Session the Town Council voted 
unanimously to open an investigation into the legality of the water ban and to direct the Town Solicitor
